To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CALR and CSFR3 mutations are the first disease-specific mutations that can be used for diagnosis of MPN.

CALR mutations are present in 70-80% of JAK2/MPL-negative ET/PMF, that CALR mutations in ET/PMF are mutually exclusive with MPL mutations, and that the CALR mutation pattern differs between ET and PMF.

CALR and CSFR mutations occur in a substantial proportion of ET and PMF patients, respectively, that CALR mutations occur in the majority of triple-negative MPNs, that CALR and JAK2 mutations have distinct clinical and biological features and that CALR mutations are associated with a better prognosis than JAK2 or triple-negative MPN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for hematopoietic malignancies and other diseases.
the discovery of novel mutations and biomarkers in myeloproliferation and their clinical relevance.
the discovery and characterization of novel mutations in MPNs, with the goal of improving diagnostic precision and drug development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the discovery of CALR and the validation of CSF3 R mutations in MPN have provided new diagnostic and therapeutic tools for patients with ET, PMF and CNL.
CALR and CSFR3 mutations are not only important diagnostic tools but also have a major prognostic impact on disease progression and survival in ET, PMF and CNL.
the discovery of CALR and, to some extent, CSF3R has improved the molecular diagnostic accuracy in myeloproliferation, but that bone marrow morphology remains a key element in the diagnostic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CALR mutations are the most important molecular marker in ET/PMF to date and that CSF3R is a highly sensitive and specific marker of CNL.

the recent discovery of CALR and the validation of CSF3 mutations have led to a significant improvement in the diagnosis of patients with ET, PMF and CNL and have provided new targets for therapeutic intervention.
the CALR mutation is a very sensitive and specific marker of JAK2/MPL negative ET/PMF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnostic criteria for MPNs should be revised to include CALR and CSFR3 mutations as well as the morphological features of prefibrotic and fibrotic PMF.
the discovery of CALR and the recent identification of CSF3RTD mutations have the potential to improve diagnostic precision in MPN.
